transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?
I’ve started to feel like I’m just not good enough at anything anymore, no matter how hard I try. It just feels like I'm failing at everything lately, and I don't know how to shake this feeling.
How long have you been feeling this way? Also, did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

This heavy feeling has been there pretty much continuously for a little over two years now. It started shortly after my husband and I began fertility treatments, which happened right around the same time I took on a lot of extra responsibilities at school, like mentoring new teachers and piloting a new curriculum.
Before these past two years, have you ever had other periods in your life lasting several weeks or months where you felt deeply down, depressed, or lost interest in things?

No, I haven't really experienced periods of feeling this deeply down or depressed before these past two years. This constant, heavy feeling really only started after we began the fertility treatments. Before that, I had my usual ups and downs, but nothing like what I've been going through lately.

Along with feeling not good enough, have you also been experiencing other changes over these past two years, such as trouble sleeping, changes in your appetite, low energy, or difficulty concentrating?

Yes, the low energy has been a huge issue for the last two years—no matter how much I sleep, I feel completely drained and have to force myself through the school day before collapsing on the couch. I haven't really noticed any major changes in my appetite or ability to concentrate, though.
During these past two years, have there been any periods lasting longer than two months where you felt like your usual self and were completely free of these symptoms?

No, there haven't been any breaks like that at all. This heavy, low mood and the feeling of just dragging myself through life has been completely continuous ever since we started the fertility treatments over two years ago. I haven't had even a couple of weeks where I felt like my usual self.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in doing things you used to enjoy, such as hobbies or spending time with family and friends?

Yes, I've really lost interest in those things and have started avoiding friends' invitations and withdrawing from our traditional Sunday family dinners. I also don't have the energy for shared activities with my husband, and even painting has just become a way to distract myself rather than something I actually enjoy.
Sometimes when people feel this heavy and exhausted for a long time, they might have thoughts of giving up. Have you experienced any thoughts of death or hurting yourself?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or wanting to end my life. Even though I feel so hopeless and completely exhausted, I've never thought about doing anything like that.

Has this low mood been a steady, low-grade background feeling throughout these two years, or have there been periods where it became much more intense and severely impacted your ability to work or function?

It has definitely been a steady, low-grade background feeling that never really lifts, rather than coming in intense spikes. I still force myself to go to work and get my teaching job done every day, but the constant exhaustion has made me withdraw at home. Because of that, I've been avoiding family dinners and letting my husband handle almost all of the household chores.
You mentioned feeling completely drained no matter how much you sleep. Have you been sleeping significantly more hours than usual, or are you having trouble falling or staying asleep?
I haven't really paid attention to the exact hours or patterns of my sleep. All I know is that no matter how much or how little sleep I get, I still wake up feeling completely exhausted.
